text: I now give the floor to his excellency
Jun Junj Ramful, Minister of Foreign
Affairs, Regional Integration and
International Trade of Maicius.
Mr. President,
allow me to congratulate his excellency
Dr. Khalilur Rahman on his election to
the presidency of the general assembly
and assure him of the support of my
delegation. I also wish to pay tribute
to his excellency Antonio Guterres for
his outstanding dedication and
commitment to this organization during
his two terms as secretary general. He
will be remembered as a leader with a
steady hand always guided by principles
of fairness, compassion and dignity for
all. Mr. President, the United Nations
has now completed the first eight
decades of its existence.
Eight decades replete with resolutions,
declarations, and action on
decolonization, development, new
international order, the new
constitution for the oceans, as well as
climate and the environment, technology,
human rights, international law, and
peacekeeping. created in the aftermath
of the second world war. The immediate
focus was obviously on peace and
security. But the UN system has evolved
significantly over the decades to expand
its scope and sphere of influence within
the confines of its charter. However,
the UN must now look to the future,
building on its record of achievements
as well as from lessons learned from
what it could not achieve. As we look to
the next 80 years, we must ask ourselves
a searching question. Is the UN fit for
the purpose for the 21st century? Not
the world of 1945, but the world of
today and beyond. We are entering a new
era of international relations defined
by unprecedented technological
developments. Often absent from the
table where the rules of Chimuru are
being adopted, developing countries risk
being left further behind. The same
exclusion afflicts the international
financial architecture which remains
skewed against the global south.
Developing nations must have a seat at
the table as equal stakeholders.
We all acknowledge that the three
pillars of the UN charter are peace and
security, development and human rights.
The twin institutional pillars provided
in the charter were and still are the
security council and ECOS as the apex
bodies for achieving these purposes.
However, over the years, optimal use has
been made primarily of only one of these
organs. We need to enhance and
accelerate the revitalization of the
general assembly and that of ECOS so
that they are not merely forums for
debate but engines of action. This must
be done as we bring about the reform of
the security council. The historical
injustice regarding the composition of
the council was acknowledged in action
39 of the pack for the future. But the
process for reform is still stalled.
Mauritius fully supports the common
African position, the eswini consensus
and the certic declaration calling for
no fewer than two permanent and five
non-permanent African seats on the
council. Mauritius also supports the
call for SIDS to have a seat on a reform
council. On the question of the veto,
Maitius allowance itself with the pulion
of a growing number of states that in
the event the veto is retained, any new
permanent member must have the same
rights as the original permanent
members. Maicius also supports the
Franco Mexican initiative on the
suspension of the veto in cases of mass
atrocities.
We support the positions of the G4 and
the L69 on council reform and we
reiterate our support for India's
candidature for a permanent seat
commenurate with its constructive role
in global affairs. Mr. President
Mauritius welcomes the increasing
recourse to the International Court of
Justice as a mechanism for the peaceful
settlement of disputes and determination
of issues of international law. We call
upon member states which have not yet
done so to accept the compulsory
jurisdiction of the ICJ. We welcome the
landmark unanimous advisory opinion of
the ICJ on the obligations of states in
respect of climate change. This was a
vindication of the tireless advocacy of
Vanuatu and the core group of states.
Mauritius was proud to stand among them.
We call for the full operization of this
advisory opinion including through the
followup action requested by this
assembly in accordance with the UN
General Assembly landmark resolution of
the 20th of May 2026. Welcoming the
advisory opinion of the international
court of justice on the obligations of
states in respect of climate change. We
also support the legal principle
affirmed by the ICG that states are
under no obligation to update their
maritime baselines or zones to account
for climate induced sea level rise.
Maitius calls for the principle that
state and sovereignty are not impacted
by sea level rise to be formally
codified.
Mr. President, water stands at the front
line of the climate crisis. Water is a
major concern globally and Maitius
welcomes the holding of the UN water
conference in December this year. We
look forward to this crucial global
issue being addressed by the
international committee community as a
matter of urgency. We also call for
enhanced, accessible and predictable
climate finance accompanied by
comprehensive capacity building and
disaster risk management for the most
vulnerable. I also wish to highlight
that Maicius is currently conducting a
constitutional review exercise which
will include giving constitutional
protection to the rights of nature. Mr.
President, the crisis in development
financing is deepening. Concessional
financing for developing countries is
declining precisely when the need is
greatest. The graduation of countries
including small island developing states
should be encouraged and supported and
not prejudice access to affordable
finance. Malaysia calls for a review of
the criteria for access to concessional
financing that reflect vulnerability
rather than income per capita alone. We
also call for the strengthening of the
rules-based multilateral trading system
and for fair, transparent and equitable
mechanisms for resolving trade disputes.
Mr. President, the rapid evolution of
digital and emerging technologies,
including artificial intelligence, is
already shaping economic, social, and
institutional developments across the
globe. We support the general assembly
resolution establishing the global
dialogue on AI governance and welcome
the work being done by the independent
international scientific panel on AI for
Maitius. Digital innovation is a
developmental imperative. We have
launched with UN support a national
artificial intelligence strategy and a
national fintech strategy. We need an
open, transparent and inclusive dialogue
on governance of the new technologies
which ensures that the benefits of
technological progress are shared
equitably and that the risks are managed
collectively.
As a coastal state with an EEZ of 2.2
million square kilometers, that is more
than 1,000 times our land mass.
Mauritius is profoundly connected to the
ocean.
We reaffirm our unwavering commitment to
UNOS as the legal framework governing
all activities in the oceans including
the seabed and subs soil beyond national
jurisdiction. We welcome the decisions
of the UN commission on the limits of
the continental shelf approving the
submission lodged by Maitius in December
208 and approved in March 2011 as well
as the second one filed in May 209 and
approved in July 2026.
We welcome the 100th ratification of the
BBJ agreement and calls for its prompt
and effective implementation. We look
forward to its first conference of the
parties advancing the institutional,
financial and procedural arrangement
necessary for the effective
implementation of the agreement.
Collaboration is key to effective
maritime security, maritime surveillance
and domain awareness. We call on the
international community to support
regional and subregional initiatives. In
this regard, I am pleased to inform that
Mauritius will with the support of the
European Union and the commission
will host a ministerial conference on
cyber crime and seekable security in the
western Indian Ocean in the first
quarter of 2027.
Mr. President Bushius welcomes the major
developments taking place across Africa
with regards to greater integration and
pooling of resources particularly in
relation to capacity building. In this
regard, Maitius has initiated action at
the UN for promoting enhanced regulatory
frameworks in developing countries
namely through pooling of resources.
Mauritius attaches great importance to
the elimination of all forms of racism,
racial discrimination and xenophobia. We
welcome the high level meeting on this
subject and reaffirm our commitment to
the international decade for people of
African descent. Maitius is fully
committed to supporting the convention
on the elimination of all forms of
discrimination against women and the
Beijing declaration and platform for
action. Earlier this year, Maitius
adopted new legislation to further
enhance the protection of women's right.
Mr. President, we are deeply concerned
by the effects of regional conflicts and
instability on development, economic
growth, food security, and the
achievement of SDGs. The crisis in the
Gulf and threats to freedom of
navigation have sent shock waves across
the global economy. for a small open
economy such as Maitius which depends on
maritime trade routes for over 90% of
its primary energies imports and more
than 70% of its food supply. These
effects are felt accurately. We call for
restraint for dialogue and for a durable
diplomatic resolution
on Palestine. Maicius reaffirms its
long-standing position in support of the
inaliable right of the Palestinian
people to self-determination and to an
independent sovereign state with East
Jerusalem as its capital. Living in
peace and security along its neighbors,
the cycle of violence must end. Too many
people have suffered for far too long.
We note with deep concern that the
establishment of unlawful settlements
may be a major obstacle to peace.
Mr. President, I now come to an issue
which for Maitius is non-negotiable.
It concerns our sovereignty over the
Shaos Islands. The agreement on the
sheos aripilago signed by Maitius and
the United Kingdom in May 2025
stands as living proof that trust in
multilateralism and UN judicial organs
can achieve the peaceful settlement of
disputes and the completion of our
nation's decolonization and restore the
rights of Maicians of Sheaggo origin by
force of law. Trust especially amongst
neighbors and in the region is
reinforced when there is respect for the
rule of law, for the resolutions of the
United Nations General Assembly, the
ruling of the international tribunal on
the law of the sea and the ICJ's
advisory opinion on the shagus
archipelago which carries authoritative
obligations.
We trust that states which laid the very
foundation of the new postwar legal
order will recommit to full respect and
compliance with international law and
correct this historical injustice
without delay. As William Award
Gladstone, a four-term former prime
British prime minister and great
campaigner for peace and freedom put it,
"Justice delayed is justice denied."
Mr. President,
>> Mr. President,
Truman Island is an integral part of the
territory of the Republic of Maitius.
We have constantly maintained our
position concerning the sovereignty of
the Republic of Maitius over this
island.
We reiterate our call upon France to
engage constructively
with a view to resolving the dispute
relating to Trumalin Island in the
spirit of friendship which characterizes
relations between our two countries.
>> Mr. President Murius is committed to
upholding the pledges made at the social
summit in Doha.
Nowhere is that promise to universal
social protection more concrete than in
our health services. As non-communicable
diseases and a rapidly aging population
place growing pressure on our health
system, we are strengthening public
health care through major investment,
improved service delivery, expanded
specialized care, and a greater focus on
prevention. Moritius will continue to
offer free and quality public health
care to each and every citizen. We thus
welcome the holding of the 2027 high
level meeting on universal health
coverage and militia stands ready to
contribute to that global effort.
Today the high level meeting on pandemic
prevention, preparedness and response
met at a decisive moment and decisive
moments demand more than mere
intentions. Maitius supports the
conclusions of the terms of benefit
sharing guaranting vulnerable countries
real access to affordable safe effective
and quality med medicines including
generics vaccines
uh diagnosis diagnostics and health
technologies. It is of crucial
importance to widen pandemic financing
eligibility including the pandemic fund
to formally incorporate the
multi-dimensional
vulnerability index. Maicius also
welcomes UN initiatives on road sa on
road safety an issue to which we attach
the highest importance and which acts as
a silent epidemic that continues to
claim far too many lives
disproportionately in developing
countries. We call for greater
international attention and resources
for this critical issue.
>> Mr. President,
we find ourselves at a critical juncture
in the history of the United Nations.
The organization is facing significant
challenges both internally and
externally.
Internally, there is the process
launched by the Secretary General to
update the administrative and financial
structure of the organization to allow
our organization to be better equipped
to overcome future challenges.
Externally, the role and the functions
of the organization
as well as the composition of its
principal organs are in doubt and need
to be redefined.
The volunt the will expressed by the
international community following the
war to create an instrument for
cooperation in order to establish a new
world order is still there. The fact
that the number of actors has more than
tripled in the past eight decades
reflects an engagement that an equitment
that is even bigger and even more
diverse than it was when the UN was
created. We are confident that the
international community
around half of which is made up of young
people that aim to protect the planet
that want to better share wealth and
aspire to use new technologies advisedly
will be able to overcome new challenges.
We reiterate our commitment to
multilateralism
as well as our confidence in its ability
to respond to people's expectations.
Thank you, Mr. President.
I thank the Minister of Foreign Affairs,
Regional Integration and International
Trade of Mauritius.
